findings.description: The 2 GiB MERGE_HEAD test grows an all-NUL sparse file. With the old `cat`, command substitution drops the NULs, MERGING comes out empty, and the hook still exits 2. So the test catches a reverted `cat` only when reading 2 GiB overruns the 4 s spawn timeout, which a fast shell might not. Writing a non-tip object id plus a newline before calling `truncateSync` would make the test independent of timing.

`head -c 66` uses a bare `66`, and the JSDoc and decision 99 never say why it is 66: 64 hex digits (SHA-256), a newline, and one more byte so an overlong value is detected. The 40/64 length checks on the next line depend on this number, so a reader changing the accepted lengths has no cue to change the 66.

In the `MERGE_OF_TARGET_SHELL` JSDoc, the line ending "…past the hook timeout. Best effort: a session" runs to about 92 columns, while the rest of the block wraps at about 80. The paragraph was only partly reflowed.

In decision 99, the line "timeout; bounding the hooks' blocking reads in time is owed. Both hooks are best effort here, not a" runs to about 103 columns, past the file's 100-column wrap. Rewrap from "Both hooks are best effort…" onward.
